citation: Schopen K, Ewald AC, Johannes BW et al. (2017). Short-Term Effects of Lupin vs. Whey Supplementation on Glucose and Insulin Responses to a Standardized Meal in a Randomized Cross-Over Trial. Frontiers in Physiology 8:198.
protocol: Three meals scaled per kg body weight, crossover: carbohydrate-rich reference meal (0.89 g/kg carbohydrate, 0.32 g/kg protein, 0.21 g/kg fat), reference + whey (0.69 g/kg protein, 0.21 fat, 0.90 carbohydrate), reference + lupin flour (0.69 protein, 0.30 fat, 0.90 carbohydrate). Blood at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 120, 180 min.
population: n=12 healthy volunteers (5 men, 7 women), aged 23-33, BMI ~21-25 kg/m2 (individual values in Table 1).

reports.where: Table 4: AUC 0-60 and 0-180 min per meal, mg·min/dL
Table 4: AUC 0-60 and 0-180 min per meal, mU·min/L

note: Paired-meal contrast, protein_source: reference meal + whey vs + lupin at matched protein and carbohydrate. Animal vs legume protein in a real mixed meal. Watch: lupin brings ~40% more fat (0.30 vs 0.21 g/kg), doses are per kg so grams need the body weights, AUCs may be total rather than incremental. Only in figures: glucose and insulin time courses.
